title: Alia Bhatt Just Joined Tumbbad 2. The Cult Horror Classic Is Now a ₹150 Crore Blockbuster.
excerpt: She'll star alongside Nawazuddin Siddiqui and Sohum Shah in the folklore sequel filming in real monsoons — and her role leads directly into Tumbbad 3.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Alia Bhatt joins *Tumbbad 2*, starring alongside Nawazuddin Siddiqui and Sohum Shah.
  • The sequel has a budget between ₹100 crore and ₹150 crore, a significant increase from the original.
  • Filming takes place during Maharashtra's monsoons to enhance authenticity.
  • The original *Tumbbad* re-released in 2024, earning over ₹40 crore at the box office.
  • The sequel is set to release on December 3, 2027.

The first Tumbbad was made on prayers and grit — a film so singular that nobody quite knew what to do with it when it arrived in 2018. It made a modest collection at the box office, earned a devoted cult following on streaming, and then did something almost unheard of: it came back. The 2024 theatrical re-release pulled in over ₹40 crore, turning an industry footnote into a franchise starter. The message was unmistakable. India was ready for more.

Now the sequel is officially here — in production, star-studded, and armed with a budget that would have been unthinkable when Sohum Shah was scraping together financing for the original a decade ago. Alia Bhatt has confirmed she's joined the cast of Tumbbad 2, starring alongside Sohum Shah and Nawazuddin Siddiqui. The film is directed by Adesh Prasad and is set to release on December 3, 2027.

!Nawazuddin Siddiqui — Photo: Wikimedia Commons

"That's what makes this opportunity so exciting." — Alia Bhatt

This isn't a casual addition."

"Tumbbad has stayed with me ever since I first watched it. Very few films create a world that feels this original and immersive, and even fewer continue to grow in people's imagination years after they've released. That's what makes this opportunity so exciting." — Alia Bhatt

This isn't a casual addition. According to reports, Alia has committed to a 20-day filming schedule for a character described as the catalyst for a major twist at the film's conclusion — one that leads directly into Tumbbad 3, where she's confirmed to take the lead alongside Sohum Shah. She's not dropping in for a cameo. She's planting a flag.

The timing is strategic. After the commercial disappointments of Jigra and Alpha — both of which struggled to recover their investments — Alia is balancing risk with reputation. Tumbbad 2 gives her the kind of credibility that box office numbers alone can't buy: a critically revered, auteur-driven franchise with genuine audience devotion. And she's pairing it with Sanjay Leela Bhansali's Love & War, scheduled for January 2027, ensuring she ends the year with both critical heat and commercial firepower.

Nawazuddin Siddiqui, meanwhile, has been signed to play a morally complex and central character. His inclusion adds a layer of intensity that the franchise hasn't had before. The actor was spotted filming during Eid, telling reporters, *"It is going to be a working festival for me."* The Tumbbad 2 team later wished him on his birthday with a cheeky nod: *"We were working with the treasure all along."* The dynamic between Nawazuddin and Sohum — two actors who build characters from the ground up, method-style — is shaping up to be the film's emotional spine.

And then there's the scale. The original Tumbbad was an underdog by every measure. The sequel is being positioned as a mainstream blockbuster, with a budget estimated between ₹100 crore and ₹150 crore — a staggering jump from the original's shoestring production. Pen Studios, the powerhouse behind RRR and Gangubai Kathiawadi, is co-producing, and their involvement signals the kind of distribution muscle that the first film never had.

!Mumbai — Photo: Wikimedia Commons

Producer Dr. Jayantilal Gada called Alia "the perfect choice" and noted this marks their third collaboration after those two blockbusters.

On the creative front, director Adesh Prasad — who co-directed and wrote the original — is chasing authenticity above spectacle. The crew has been filming during the natural Maharashtra monsoons to recreate the franchise's signature gloom without artificial rain setups. They've built a massive 7-to-8-acre set in Mumbai for the first schedule, deployed over 1,600 crew members and junior artists for one of Indian cinema's biggest crowd-driven scenes, and brought in prosthetic designer Shaune Harrison to craft three distinct looks for a main character.

The tagline says it all: #PralayAayega — The apocalypse is coming.

For diaspora audiences who discovered Tumbbad through late-night streaming binges or its viral re-release buzz, the wait for the theatrical experience comes down to one date: December 3, 2027. With Alia Bhatt stepping into a world this dark, this strange, and this distinctly Indian, the sequel is no longer just a cult follow-up.

It's an event.
